Almost every mutation here is a constant, because that is what this dispatch is -- the arms hold no arithmetic.  What the set has to prove is that each of the seven arms is separately driven, that the five branches out of the table's own range are reached, and that the three signedness decisions in the tail are the ones the object makes.  IT NOW ANCHORS INTO `src/pump/v34/v34hshak.c`.  The set was written against `src/pump/v34/v34hstxblock.c`, the third of three reconstructions of this dispatch; finding F591 collapsed that file onto `t3m_txblock`/`t3m_tail` and every anchor was rewritten to the survivor's spelling -- `obj->progress` to `*f->progress`, `TB_INT(obj, TB_F2218)` to `T3M_I32(f, T3M_MODE)`, and so on -- with the claim each makes unchanged.  Twenty-six of them share their find text with an anchor in `v34hst3mid` or `v34hst3core`; that is not a duplicate, because the binary is what a mutation set is tested by and `t_v34hstbl2` is the only one that drives table 2's arms directly.

the txstate reload at 0x62b5f, taken out
why: 0x62b5f reloads +0x3596 into %cx before rejoining the tail -- the block entered at 0x62b45, whose `movzwl 0x3596(%ebx),%ecx` is at 0x62b5f (592 re-fixes the address 550's table header moved), and `t3m_tail` models it -- which is the one thing the reconstruction this set was written against could not, its entry taking only the object.  Taking it out is still equivalent IN THIS TREE, and that is measured rather than argued: every one of the forty-odd sites that reaches the dispatch either passes the object's own +0x3596 or, in arms 48 and 63, stores the value into +0x3596 before passing it, so the reloaded and the passed txstate are equal everywhere.  Removing it was run against all eight suites that touch this file and NOT CAUGHT by any of them (591).  It stops being equivalent the first time an arm passes a value it did not store while +0x3596 holds 0x4a, 0x52, 0x53 or 0x54 -- which is why the parameter exists.  Held fixed: nothing.

label: txstate held zero-extended rather than sign-extended
why: The object spells the state two ways -- `cmp $0x4a,%cx` zero-extended at 0x62a70 and `movswl %cx,%eax` sign-extended at 0x62ac5 -- and one `short` models both.  Every test the two spellings feed is equality against a small positive constant, which agrees for all 65,536 halfwords; the one inequality, `> 0x53` at 0x62acd, only decides whether to test equality with 0x54, which is false either way -- unsigned it takes the `> 0x53` branch and fails `== 0x54`, signed it takes the `else` and fails `== 0x52`, and both leave +0x0004 alone.  So this is equivalent over the WHOLE range and not merely over the 0..86 the diagnostics allow.  The anchor is now the tail's parameter rather than the dispatch's local, which is the same claim about the same halfword.  Held fixed: nothing.
